root_cause.text: wait_sb_inodes() in fs/writeback unconditionally waited on PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK inodes without excluding address_space mappings that provide no data-integrity semantics, so FUSE writeback-cache inodes could block sync forever on stalled userspace writeback.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY mapping flag, sets it for FUSE writeback-cache mappings in fuse_init_file_inode(), and changes wait_sb_inodes() to skip mappings when mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping) is true; the commit message explicitly says faulty FUSE servers that do not reply to writes caused wait_sb_inodes() to “wait forever” and that syncs for fuse were traditionally no-ops.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid waiting for writeback completion in wait_sb_inodes() for mappings without data integrity guarantees.
intent_record.what: The condition that skips mappings in wait_sb_inodes() was expanded from only checking !mapping_tagged(mapping, PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK) to also skip when mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping) is true, and a comment was added explaining that such mappings do not need to be waited on.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will no longer wait for writeback completion on mappings that lack data integrity semantics, even if they are tagged for writeback, reducing unnecessary waiting because those mappings cannot guarantee persistent storage anyway.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark FUSE file mappings as lacking data integrity when writeback cache is enabled to correct inode mapping behavior in that mode.
intent_record.what: The change adds braces around the existing `if (fc->writeback_cache)` block in `fuse_init_file_inode()` and inserts a second call inside it: `mapping_set_no_data_integrity(&inode->i_data);` after `mapping_set_writeback_may_deadlock_on_reclaim(&inode->i_data);`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when FUSE writeback caching is enabled, the inode's address space is now additionally marked with no data integrity support, alongside the existing writeback reclaim deadlock flag. This changes the mapping behavior for such inodes so the kernel will treat data integrity operations differently under writeback cache mode.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new mapping flag to identify address_space instances that do not guarantee data integrity.
intent_record.what: A new enum constant, AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY = 11, was added to enum mapping_flags with the comment "no data integrity guarantees".
intent_record.how: This introduces a new address_space mapping flag value that can be used elsewhere in the kernel to mark mappings that do not provide data integrity guarantees, enabling later runtime checks or behavior selection based on that property, without changing behavior by itself in this hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add inline helpers to set and test the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag on an address_space mapping.
intent_record.what: Two new static inline helpers were added for struct address_space: mapping_set_no_data_integrity(), which sets the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY bit in mapping->flags, and mapping_no_data_integrity(), which returns whether that bit is set via test_bit().
intent_record.how: This introduces a standard accessor API for marking an address_space as not providing data integrity semantics and for querying that state at runtime, enabling other code to consistently set and check the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag through dedicated helpers.

grouping_result.intent: Mark FUSE file mappings as lacking data integrity when writeback cache is enabled to correct inode mapping behavior in that mode.
Add inline helpers to set and test the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag on an address_space mapping.

consistency_review.core_intent: Adjust inode writeback/wait behavior for filesystems like FUSE operating without data integrity guarantees, especially when writeback cache is enabled.
Add support for marking address_space mappings as not guaranteeing data integrity by introducing a new flag and inline helpers to set and test it.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause: they stop wait_sb_inodes() from waiting on mappings that lack data-integrity semantics and mark FUSE writeback-cache mappings accordingly, preventing the indefinite sync wait described.

The root cause is that wait_sb_inodes() did not exclude mappings with no data-integrity semantics. This group introduces exactly the address_space flag and helpers needed to mark and detect such mappings, which is a direct prerequisite to excluding them from the wait logic.

candidates.rationale: This conditional only skips mappings that are not tagged for writeback, but before the fix it did not exclude mappings lacking data-integrity semantics. As a result, wait_sb_inodes() would still wait on tagged FUSE writeback-cache inodes and could block indefinitely.

When writeback_cache was enabled, FUSE marked mappings only as potentially deadlocking on reclaim, but did not mark them as lacking data integrity. This omission allowed such mappings to be treated like integrity-relevant writeback in wait_sb_inodes(), contributing to the indefinite wait.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition caused wait_sb_inodes() to wait on any mapping tagged with PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK, without excluding mappings that do not provide data-integrity semantics. That allowed FUSE writeback-cache inodes to be included in sync waiting and potentially block forever on stalled userspace writeback.

In FUSE writeback-cache mode this statement marked the mapping as reclaim-problematic but did not mark it as lacking data integrity. Because of that omission, the mapping was still treated as integrity-relevant by wait_sb_inodes(), contributing to the indefinite wait on FUSE writeback.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of wait_sb_inodes(), which is the function named in the root cause, so it is sufficient to judge. The vulnerable construct is still present: the function explicitly waits on every inode on the superblock writeback list solely based on generic writeback tagging, with no exclusion for mappings that do not provide data-integrity semantics. In particular, inside the loop it does `if (!mapping_tagged(mapping, PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK)) continue;` and then calls `filemap_fdatawait_keep_errors(mapping);`. There is no check of the mapping's backing a_ops / data-integrity capability before waiting. The root cause says wait_sb_inodes() 'unconditionally waited on PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK inodes without excluding address_space mappings that provide no data-integrity semantics'; that is exactly what this code does. The commit changes traversal from `sb->s_inodes` to `sb->s_inodes_wb`, but this is only a performance/list-management change (`list_splice_init(&sb->s_inodes_wb, &sync_list)`, iterating `i_wb_list`). It does not add any filtering to avoid waiting on FUSE writeback-cache or other non-data-integrity mappings. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present and the fix is not yet in this function.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it directly shows the relevant writeback semantics on FUSE inode mappings. The root cause is that sync/wait_sb_inodes() can wait forever on mappings that do not advertise reclaim-deadlock-prone writeback behavior unless they are properly marked. This commit explicitly adds that handling in fuse_init_file_inode(): `if (fc->writeback_cache) mapping_set_writeback_may_deadlock_on_reclaim(&inode->i_data);`. That means FUSE writeback-cache mappings are now marked with the address_space flag described in the commit message (`AS_WRITEBACK_MAY_DEADLOCK_ON_RECLAIM`). The rest of the diff is consistent with switching FUSE over to normal VM writeback tracking: custom writeback tracking helpers are removed (`fuse_range_is_writeback`, `fuse_wait_on_page_writeback`, `fuse_wait_on_folio_writeback`, rb-tree bookkeeping), and standard helpers are used instead, e.g. `folio_wait_writeback(...)` and `filemap_range_has_writeback(...)`. Since the vulnerable condition was unmarked FUSE writeback-cache mappings causing global sync to wait forever, and this version marks such mappings correctly, the vulnerable construct is not present here and the fix is present.
